report.summary: Reviewed only the supplied seven-file packet against the plan's three cycles. Cycle 1 (citation-ID catalog) is feasible in principle, but the packet shows concrete traps that a minimal implementation must close: the legacy decoder (assessment-completion.ts:26-38) cannot tell a v2 request apart from a v1 request, so 'no auto fallback' cannot hold; the model-visible ID schema must stay enumerated and non-strict, because strict mode rejects enum values that are absent from the catalog (assessment-completion.ts:61-81); and every catalogId/entry-ID mismatch must be rejected by exact comparison, not weakest-link logic. The current v1 path silently accepts repeated-copy ambiguity: sent[file].indexOf(excerpt) takes the first occurrence (delivery-assessment.ts:89), and the v2 proposal's offset resolution must reject ambiguity rather than repeat indexOf. Cycle 2's page/block witness needs an explicit ordered checkpoint over every saved business check plus every page in the locked list, because the current per-criterion aggregation buckets unknowns into a non-blocking reason string (source-business-evidence.ts:91, 102-104). Cycle 3's tr relation is bounded, but the 'two-cell' requirement conflicts with the existing label-prefix single-leaf model (source-business-evidence.ts:28, 83-86). It also leaves unresolved whether tr ownership is joined to the already-saved locked source list and file identity. No runtime checks, builds or tests were run. All findings are source-reading inferences and are labelled as such.

findings.title: Legacy JSON decoder remains reachable for the proposed v2 function, so 'no auto fallback' is not enforceable as stated
findings.evidence: assessmentCompletionText returns {transport:'legacy_json'} whenever finish_reason==='stop' and message.tool_calls is absent or empty (lines 26-31). The tool name is checked only on the tool_calls branch (line 37). assessmentReportJson accepts legacy text with trailing-brace repair disabled (line 52). delivery-assessment.ts:206 then parses whatever envelope is returned and never inspects completion.transport (lines 206-209, 301 writes method 'source-ai-v1' either way). A v2 request that names a new function v2 therefore can receive a legacy-style items/citations reply and be validated as if it were the same contract. That is an implicit fallback inside the same call, which contradicts plan line 20 ('No auto fallback request/retry') and guarantees that some live provider reports do not use IDs.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): send a v2 tool_choice for submit_source_assessment_v2; the provider returns choice.finish_reason='stop' with message.content holding the old items[]/citations file/excerpt JSON and no tool_calls. assessmentCompletionText line 31 returns transport='legacy_json'. The v2 caller, if it reuses this decoder without a transport guard, parses it and returns a report with method unchanged, which is indistinguishable from a strict v2 answer and shows no 'legacy' diagnostic.
findings.suggestion: Have the v2 decoder accept only transport==='strict_tool' with fn.name===the v2 name and reject every other envelope. Keep assessmentCompletionText's legacy branch reachable only from an explicit legacy entry point that writes a separate method/diagnostic value (for example 'source-ai-v1-legacy') so the stored report states truthfully which wire format was used.

findings.title: First-occurrence indexOf binding is the repeated-occurrence trap the catalog must replace, and the current citation validator cannot express offsets
findings.evidence: citations() binds a model quote with sent[file].indexOf(excerpt) and stores start/end from that first hit (lines 89-91). If a page holds two identical price rows or two identical labels, a citation of the second copy is silently credited to the first. Label coverage downstream (assessment-label-citations.ts:76) accepts any citation span that contains the label span, so the wrong copy still yields 'covered'. The plan's 'first only vs. full repeated occurrence offsets (plan line 19, 'never indexOf rebinds repeated copy') is therefore not just an improvement: it is the correction for a real ambiguity in the evidence model. The existing ProofAssessmentCitation carries only file/start/end/excerpt (as consumed at lines 61, 89-91, 280), with no slot for the original wire ID or the catalog entry.
findings.reproduction:
Reasoning trace (unexecuted): menu.html has
  • Tea AUD 18
    • twice, at offsets a and b, with the second row's price wrong in a variant. The model returns excerpt 'Tea AUD 18' intending the second row. Line 89 resolves start=a. The business check looks at leaves, not at citation offsets, so the diagnostic points at the correct leaf, but the saved citation start/end describes the first row. Any future page/block witness built on citation offsets would be wrong.
findings.suggestion: In v2, look up entries by catalogId and entry ID in a frozen map, and require the entry's recorded start/end/excerpt to equal the stored catalog entry exactly. Attach the original wire ID and resolved offsets as separate diagnostic fields beside the unchanged ProofAssessmentCitation, so the saved schema is preserved. Reject an ID whose entry is unknown, duplicated or stale, and never fall back to text search.

findings.title: Enum-based citation schema must be kept non-strict for v2, and file/catalog mismatch must reject rather than take the weakest link
findings.evidence: The strict tool schema enumerates file: {enum:[...sourceFiles]} and the criterion IDs (lines 70, 72, 77 strict:true). If v2 entry IDs are added as a nonempty enum of short IDs, strict mode will reject a model that simply does not cite every entry, and strict-mode providers may refuse enum values not used in the reply. The plan (line 19) requires 'strict new named function v2 returns catalogId and citations as entry-ID arrays'. It must say explicitly that the v2 definition is non-strict, like the existing item/risk/limitation cardinals (line 68 comment, lines 79-81 descriptions). Also, requiring both catalogId and per-entry keys means the validator must compare key syntax, not just 'resolvable'. The current citations() pattern (delivery-assessment.ts:86-88) requires keys to match exactly, which is the right model.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): if v2 copies line 77 with strict:true and an enum of 2,000 entry IDs, an answer citing one ID per item may fail provider-side strict validation with a schema error. If a mixed reply has catalogId=hashA but entry IDs from catalog hashB, a validator that resolves each ID independently could accept it as long as both maps exist in the freeze.
findings.suggestion: Define the v2 tool as a named function with strict:false and plain string pattern for entry IDs, validating membership locally. Validate that catalogId equals the frozen ID exactly and that every entry ID resolves within that same catalog. Reject any mixed, duplicate, unknown, stale or wrong-catalog ID as one dedicated failure kind, and record original and resolved values in the diagnostic.

findings.title: Cycle 2 'witness every locked file/block' needs an explicit page/checkpoint enumeration; the current aggregation hides per-check gaps
findings.evidence: createSourceBusinessEvidenceCheck aggregates checks with find-first across mismatch, then unknown (line 91). Unknown means insufficient_evidence in delivery-assessment.ts:245-247. That is the right fail-closed status but it only says 'not all checks matched'. reason strings such as 'literal_not_unique_or_not_located' (line 77) and 'complex_or_unlocated_item' (line 84) do not identify which page or block was not witnessed, and sourceBusinessEvidenceExplanation (lines 102-104) gives a single generic sentence. The plan's cycle 2 (line 26) requires full witness of every locked file/block with a gap explanation, and locally-unchanged-but-wrong-witness to become unknown. That needs a deterministic list of locked pages, not just the checks that exist. Nothing in this function enumerates the locked page list when a criterion has no saved check.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): a criterion has 3 saved checks across about.html and menu.html. If only about.html parses and menu.html is cited by the model but menu.html's check is filtered out upstream (dedup at line 63 by checkId), or if the model cites a header-only excerpt of menu.html, the current code returns 'unchanged' when the remaining about.html check matches (line 91), provided no model-unsupported status intervenes. 'Supported' at delivery-assessment.ts:243 is therefore not proof that every locked page/block was witnessed.
findings.suggestion: Return the per-check results (already produced) to the caller and compute a cycle-2 witness verdict over (a) all saved checkIds, (b) every locked page in savedBusinessSteps, and (c) any page the model citation names. Map each page/block to witnessed or unknown with a reason. Make any unknown non-unchanged. Preserve the existing changes_suggested + exact-source path for mismatches and never emit a 'missing delivery' claim for unknown.

findings.title: Cycle 3 'two-cell table row' is not expressible under the current single-leaf label-prefix rule, and tr ownership must be tied to the saved locked pair
findings.evidence: Price parsing requires exactly one leaf whose text starts with the label, the rest of that same leaf being ISO money (lines 83-86). The leaf collector accepts only p/li elements whose children are all text nodes (line 28). A two-cell tr (for example TeaAUD 18) produces no leaf, and cell children are skipped because a table is marked hidden/compound for its descendants (line 37). Unknown is the correct current fail-closed outcome (plan line 13 says this is not a false pass), but the plan's cycle 3 (line 30) proposes to support it without stating how the tr is joined to the confirmed file and unique label. 'Nested/repeated/ambiguous stay unknown' is stated but not operationalised.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): a menu.html row TeaAUD 18 yields leaves=[] (line 28 excludes tr; line 37 descends but no p/li exists). label occurrences in bodyText are 0 because bodyText is joined only from leaves (line 22 pushes text only when body is set, and line 39 joins only leaves' text). The result is unknown('label_not_unique_or_not_located') at line 82, never a supported or mismatch judgment.
findings.suggestion: For cycle 3, add a dedicated tr recognizer that accepts only a direct-child pair (one label cell + one money cell) which is unique in its table and file. It must bind to one saved check (file, label, currency, amountMinor) and record the tr's source span. Reject nested tables, rowspan/colspan, repeated labels, and any tr not in the confirmed file list, as unknown with a distinct reason.

findings.title: v2 output budget: ID arrays are smaller, but the unchanged 30,000-char completion cap and 6,400-token ceiling must be explicitly re-frozen
findings.evidence: The plan (line 19) requires the request byte bound (850,000) and the 'full-packet admission' (delivery-assessment.ts:197-198, MAX_REQUEST_UTF8_BYTES line 24) to remain. It does not state the v2 completion cap. text(completion.text, 30_000) at delivery-assessment.ts:207 and the assessmentReportJson length check (line 48) are unchanged v1 constants; MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is 6,400 (line 25). The v2 catalog adds a model-visible catalog block in the request, so catalog size must be included in the same 850,000/1,000,000 admission check and must fail closed with no truncation.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): a delivery at 840 KB of HTML/CSS passes today's line 197 check. If the catalog text (entry IDs, offsets, short excerpts) is appended without re-checking requestBytes, the combined prompt exceeds 850,000 and the check silently admits an oversized request, or else the new prompt is omitted. Either way the full-packet admission is no longer enforced exactly as written.
findings.suggestion: Compute requestBytes after inserting the catalog, require requestBytes <= MAX_REQUEST_UTF8_BYTES, and reject with ASSESSMENT_CONTEXT_LIMIT before the provider call. Keep the 30,000-char completion cap; keep output token limit unchanged or re-derive it and record it in the frozen diagnostics.

findings.title: Word-boundary occurrence counting in the catalog span selection could disagree with tr/p/li witness resolution
findings.evidence: occurrences() counts non-alphanumeric-bounded matches (lines 41-50). That is used for uniqueness at lines 76-77 and 82. The plan's catalog spans for h1/title/label/p/li/tr (line 18) will need the same rule, or model IDs and the saved check witnesses will diverge. For example, 'Tea' inside 'Teal' is not counted (the trailing 'l' is alphanumeric), while 'AUD 18' inside 'AUD 180' is not counted but 'AUD 18.0' is counted (both digits boundary on the last '0'/'8'). This is fragile for prices.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): a page contains 'AUD 18.0' and 'AUD 18'. occurrences('AUD 18') counts both because the character after '8' is '.' for the first and end-of-string for the second, so both pass the boundary check. The label check at line 82 then reports label_not_unique for a page with one true price row plus a superseded variant.
findings.suggestion: Reuse one exported literal-match function for the catalog and for the witness checks. Have the price witness require a full-cell amount() match (lines 51-57) rather than a substring boundary, so '18.0' is not silently treated as '18'.

findings.title: Plan omits that the trailing-brace repair diagnostic will also appear on ID-based reports
findings.evidence: assessmentReportJson performs a one-brace repair only for strict_tool transport (lines 51-57). If v2 reuses it, the appended limitation at delivery-assessment.ts:291-293 applies verbatim. The plan's cycle 1 (line 20) says 'Add catalog-format note only on ID reports', but it does not say how the system-inserted diagnostics (catalog-format note, ignored nulls, repair note, full-input limitation at lines 294-299) are ordered and whether the 8-limitation cap applies before or after system notes. The v1 code appends system notes past the 8-item cap without re-checking.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): a v2 reply has 8 model limitations plus a repair and an ignored-null note. output.limitations gets 10 entries (lines 291-299). The stored report has more limitations than the schema description allows. This is a fidelity diagnostic issue, not a money/acceptance one.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly that system diagnostics go into a separate frozen diagnostics field (or a clearly labelled appended list not subject to the model's 8 cap), and in v2 records the original wire transport, catalogId, and resolved offsets; keep model limitations capped at 8 before appending.

limitations: Read-only source review only; no code was executed, no provider calls were made, and no typecheck or test was run. Claims about validator behaviour are source-reading inferences.

The packet lacks contracts.ts, exact-copy-evidence.ts, source-literal-directive.ts, business-checks.ts, assessment-evidence-scope.ts, providers.ts and static-project.ts, so the ProofAssessment/ProofAssessmentCitation/ProofBusinessCheckStep shapes, getBusinessCheckPlan's page list, and provider requestJson error mapping are inferred from call sites (delivery-assessment.ts:1, 89-91, 123-132, 200-204; source-business-evidence.ts:2).

The packet also lacks the saved-schema consumers (storage/API/UI, the method field usage, reference eval fixtures). Compatibility of 'Preserve saved ProofAssessment schema' with stored reports and legacy migration is unverified.

No actual provider wire behaviour was observed. Whether the real DeepSeek endpoint honours strict:false with named v2 and whether some provider reports use IDs cannot be claimed. The plan's line 20 wording describes that as a possibility, not a fact.

Award evidence (plan lines 3-8) was not fetched or verified.
